column4: The reasoning initially specifies Family "1" -- "1" Patient : headOfFamily, whereas the final code uses Family "0..1" -- "1" Patient. The multiplicity at the Family end changes from exactly one to zero or one.

The reasoning specifies that every Dish contains 1..* Ingredients and an Ingredient may occur in 0..* Dishes. The code places 1..* at the Dish end and 0..* at the Ingredient end, reversing both multiplicities.

The reasoning states that each Customer has exactly one associated DeliveryCenter, while one DeliveryCenter may serve 0..* customers. However, the code uses Customer "1" -- "0..*" DeliveryCenter, which expresses the reverse: each delivery center is associated with one customer, while a customer may be associated with multiple delivery centers.

The reasoning specifies that each Furniture item contains 1..* Components, while each Component may be used in 0..* Furniture items. The code places 1..* at the Furniture end and 0..* at the Component end, reversing both intended multiplicities.

The reasoning states that a Rental has 0..1 actual Bike, while a Bike may be used in 0..* Rentals over time. The final code places these multiplicities at the opposite association ends, reversing the intended cardinalities.

The reasoning states that a User can have many borrowing records and a Book can also have many borrowing records over time. However, the final association places multiplicity 1 at the User end, implying that each Book can be associated with only one User across its borrowing history.
